units.translation: Etymologicum Magnum p. 341, 5. ἐνηλύσια [places struck by lightning]: εὐκίνητα [easily moved], and ἤλυσιν [a coming] for ἔλευσιν [a coming]. Aeschylus in the Argives (fr. 15) "Καπανεύς μου καταλείπεται λοιποῖς ἀκέραυνος ἀρούρων (ἀρόρων in two codices) ἐπηλυσίων (ἐνηλυσίων Stanley) ἀπέλιπεν [Capaneus is left to me, unthundered, among the remaining (fields) of the lands of approach]." Others say the places struck by lightning. Thus in the rhetorical lexicon. But in the etymologists I found: ἐνηλύσια [places struck by lightning] are called those into which a thunderbolt has entered (he uses this word because of the etymology of the word ἐνηλύσια), which are also dedicated to Zeus Kataibates and are called ἄδυτα [shrines not to be entered] and ἄβατα [places not to be trodden]. The poet's words are corrupt. Hesychius: ἐνηλύσια [places struck by lightning]: the places struck by lightning are called ἐνηλύσια, but some say εὐκίνητα [easily moved], from ἔλευσιν [a coming]. ἐνηλύσιος [one struck by lightning]: ἐμβρόντητος [thunderstruck], κεραυνόβλητος [struck by lightning].
